verified_context: Background decryption uses available private keys and already cached message sources, with the encrypted-search setting enabled. A failed attempt waits for an explicit open or a later setting reset; do not promise every downloaded message decrypts.

Disabling encrypted search logically removes decrypted text, snippets, attachment metadata and protected-subject replacements from the index/list; it restores the outer subject. This is not a secure-erasure claim. The setting defaults on.
Agent message/attachment access refuses encrypted content; the agent envelope can still contain outer sender/recipient/date/subject fields. Do not say agents have no metadata access.

Address lookup tries the address domain WKD first, then keys.openpgp.org when enabled. Explicit key-handle lookup sends a fingerprint/key ID instead of an email address. The keyserver switch does not disable domain lookup. UI/help source says only an address is sent; account for the separate identifier-lookup route during review.

List encrypted/signed marks classify message protection, not signature validity or verified ownership. ListEncrypted is the preview/status placeholder when there is no decrypted snippet. Protected-subject and preview storage depends on the indexing setting.

New-mail notification code always substitutes ListEncrypted for encrypted messages, independently of subsequent decryption. The list placeholder is conditional on a missing decrypted snippet. Translate these as distinct conditions.
